title: Chemical Reactions and Equations
source: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch.1 (ncert.nic.in jesc101, Reprint 2026-27)

questions.text: Why should a magnesium ribbon be cleaned before burning in air? Write the balanced chemical equation for the reaction that takes place.

points.text: A layer of magnesium oxide (or basic magnesium carbonate) forms on the ribbon's surface.
Cleaning removes this layer so the magnesium is exposed and burns properly.
Balanced equation: 2Mg + O2 -> 2MgO.

questions.text: What is a combination reaction? Give one example with a balanced chemical equation.

points.text: Two or more reactants combine to form a single product.
Correct example named (e.g. burning of magnesium, formation of water, calcium oxide with water).
Balanced equation for the example, e.g. CaO + H2O -> Ca(OH)2 or 2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O.

questions.text: What is a decomposition reaction? Name and explain its types, giving one balanced equation for each.

points.text: Definition: a single reactant breaks down into two or more products.
Thermal decomposition: caused by heat. Example: CaCO3 -> CaO + CO2 (or similar).
Electrolytic decomposition: caused by electricity. Example: 2H2O -> 2H2 + O2.
Photolytic decomposition: caused by light. Example: 2AgCl -> 2Ag + Cl2 (or AgBr).
Balanced equations written correctly for the examples given.

questions.text: Why is respiration considered an exothermic reaction? Explain.

points.text: Exothermic means a reaction that releases heat/energy.
During digestion, food (carbohydrates/glucose) is broken down.
Glucose combines with oxygen to give carbon dioxide, water and energy, so respiration is exothermic.

questions.text: What is a displacement reaction? Give one example with a balanced equation.

points.text: A more reactive element displaces a less reactive element from its compound/solution.
Example with balanced equation, e.g. Fe + CuSO4 -> FeSO4 + Cu.

questions.text: What is corrosion? Explain rusting of iron and write two methods to prevent it.

points.text: Corrosion: slow eating away of a metal by air/moisture/chemicals around it.
Rusting: iron reacts with oxygen and moisture to form hydrated iron oxide (rust, Fe2O3.xH2O).
Prevention: painting/oiling/greasing or galvanisation (zinc coating).

questions.text: What is rancidity? Give two methods to prevent it.

points.text: Rancidity: oxidation of oils/fats in food, giving bad smell and taste.
Prevention: airtight containers / refrigeration.
Prevention: adding antioxidants (BHA/BHT) or flushing packets with nitrogen.

questions.text: In the reaction CuO + H2 -> Cu + H2O, which substance is oxidised and which is reduced? Define both terms.

points.text: Oxidation = gain of oxygen (or loss of hydrogen).
Reduction = loss of oxygen (or gain of hydrogen).
H2 is oxidised to H2O; CuO is reduced to Cu. It is a redox reaction.

questions.text: Balance: Fe + H2O -> Fe3O4 + H2. Name the type of reaction.

points.text: Balanced: 3Fe + 4H2O -> Fe3O4 + 4H2.
It is a displacement reaction (iron displaces hydrogen from water/steam).

pyqs.repeatNote: Reaction-type identification appeared in both 2024-25 (Q21) and 2025-26 (Q27 variant) papers.
pyqs.source: CBSE Sample Paper 2024-25, Q21 (official marking scheme)
pyqs.text: Identify the type of each reaction, stating the reason: A. Fe2O3 + 2Al -> Al2O3 + 2Fe + heat   B. Pb(NO3)2 + 2KI -> PbI2 + 2KNO3

points.text: A is an exothermic displacement / redox reaction.
Reason: heat is evolved / Al (more reactive) displaces Fe / aluminium reduces iron oxide.
B is a double displacement / precipitation reaction.
Reason: exchange of ions / yellow precipitate of lead iodide (PbI2) forms.

pyqs.repeatNote: Electrolysis of water appears in 2025-26 (Q27); not in the 2024-25 paper, so not tagged repeated.
pyqs.source: CBSE Sample Paper 2025-26, Q27 (official marking scheme)
pyqs.text: Amrita passed electricity through distilled water but the bulb did not glow. She then added a substance for electrolysis. A. Which gas forms at the anode and which at the cathode? B. Why did the bulb not glow with distilled water? C. Which substance did she add?

points.text: Oxygen at the anode, hydrogen at the cathode.
Distilled water is a poor conductor of electricity.
She added a few drops of H2SO4 (or NaCl / any strong electrolyte).

pyqs.repeatNote: Metal-salt displacement with CuSO4 appeared in both 2024-25 (Q5, lead) and 2025-26 (Q19, iron nail).
pyqs.source: CBSE Sample Paper 2025-26, Q19 (MCQ, official marking scheme)
pyqs.text: An iron nail is added to test tube P (aqueous copper(II) sulphate) and Q (aqueous silver nitrate). The correct observation is: (official answer: brown coating in P, silver coating in Q - explain WHY both reactions happen)

points.text: Iron is more reactive than copper and silver, so it displaces both from their salt solutions.
Fe + CuSO4 -> FeSO4 + Cu (brown copper coating); Fe + 2AgNO3 -> Fe(NO3)2 + 2Ag (silver coating).

pyqs.repeatNote: Metal-salt displacement with CuSO4 appeared in both 2024-25 (Q5, lead) and 2025-26 (Q19, iron nail).
pyqs.source: CBSE Sample Paper 2024-25, Q5 (MCQ, official marking scheme)
pyqs.text: When lead powder is added to blue copper sulphate solution, after a few hours the solution becomes colourless. What type of reaction is this, and why does the colour disappear? (official answer: displacement)

points.text: It is a displacement reaction.
Lead (more reactive) displaces copper: Pb + CuSO4 -> PbSO4 + Cu, so blue CuSO4 is used up and the colour disappears.

pyqs.repeatNote: Exo/endothermic identification appeared in both years (2024-25 Q7; 2025-26 Q27 variant tags 2Mg+O2 as exothermic and ZnCO3 as endothermic).
pyqs.source: CBSE Sample Paper 2024-25, Q7 (MCQ, official marking scheme)
pyqs.text: Which of these is an endothermic reaction - burning a candle, cooking food, decomposition of vegetable matter, or sodium reacting with air? Explain what makes it endothermic. (official answer: cooking of food)

points.text: Cooking of food is endothermic.
It absorbs heat from outside (heat must be supplied continuously); the others release heat, so they are exothermic.

kb.question: Why do we balance chemical equations?
kb.answer: Ek reaction mein atoms na bante hain na mit te hain (law of conservation of mass). Isliye dono side har element ke atoms equal hone chahiye - isi ko balancing kehte hain. Unbalanced equation galat hota hai kyunki woh mass conserve nahi karta.
kb.source: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch.1 §1.1.2 (law of conservation of mass)

kb.question: What is a combination reaction?
kb.answer: Jab 2 ya zyada reactants milke SIRF EK product banate hain, woh combination reaction hai. Example: CaO + H2O -> Ca(OH)2 (quicklime + paani = slaked lime). Yaad rakho: A + B -> AB.
kb.source: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch.1 (Eq. 1.13 and after)

kb.question: What is a decomposition reaction?
kb.answer: Isme EK reactant toot ke 2 ya zyada products banata hai - combination ka ulta. 3 types: thermal (heat se, jaise CaCO3 -> CaO + CO2), electrolytic (electricity se, jaise 2H2O -> 2H2 + O2), photolytic (light se, jaise 2AgCl -> 2Ag + Cl2).

kb.question: What is a displacement reaction?
kb.answer: Zyada reactive element kam reactive element ko uske compound se hata deta hai. Example: Fe + CuSO4 -> FeSO4 + Cu - iron nail blue copper sulphate solution mein daalo, solution green ho jata hai aur nail pe brown copper jamta hai.
kb.source: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch.1, Activity 1.9 (iron nail in CuSO4)

kb.question: What is a double displacement / precipitation reaction?
kb.answer: Do compounds apne ions exchange karte hain. Agar ek product insoluble solid (precipitate) bane toh use precipitation reaction bhi kehte hain. Example: Na2SO4 + BaCl2 -> BaSO4 (white ppt) + 2NaCl.
kb.source: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch.1, Activity 1.10 (Na2SO4 + BaCl2)

kb.question: Exothermic vs endothermic?
kb.answer: Exothermic = heat RELEASE hoti hai (jalna, respiration, CaO + paani). Endothermic = heat ABSORB hoti hai (CaCO3 ko heat karna, photosynthesis). Exam tip: 'exo' = exit, heat bahar nikalti hai.

kb.question: What are oxidation and reduction?
kb.answer: Oxidation = oxygen ka judna YA hydrogen ka nikalna. Reduction = oxygen ka nikalna YA hydrogen ka judna. Dono saath mein hote hain - isliye 'redox' reaction. Example: CuO + H2 -> Cu + H2O mein CuO reduce hota hai, H2 oxidise hota hai.

kb.question: What is rancidity?
kb.answer: Jab oil/fat wale food hawa ke oxygen se react karke kharaab smell aur taste de dete hain, use rancidity kehte hain. Rokne ke liye: airtight container, antioxidants (BHA/BHT), ya chips packet mein nitrogen gas bharna.

kb.question: What is corrosion and rusting?
kb.answer: Metal ka dheere-dheere hawa/moisture se react karke kharab hona corrosion hai. Iron ka corrosion = rusting (brown rust, Fe2O3.xH2O). Rokne ke liye painting, oiling, galvanisation (zinc coating) karte hain.
kb.source: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch.1 §1.3.1 (prevention detail from Ch.3)

kb.question: Why clean magnesium ribbon before burning?
kb.answer: Ribbon ke surface pe magnesium oxide ki layer jam jati hai jo burning rokti hai. Sandpaper se saaf karne se pure magnesium expose hota hai aur woh aache se jalta hai: 2Mg + O2 -> 2MgO (dazzling white light).

kb.question: Why is respiration exothermic?
kb.answer: Digestion mein carbohydrates glucose mein tootte hain. Glucose oxygen ke saath react karke CO2 + water + ENERGY deta hai. Energy release ho rahi hai, isliye respiration exothermic reaction hai.

kb.question: Quicklime, slaked lime and whitewashing?
kb.answer: CaO (quicklime) + H2O -> Ca(OH)2 (slaked lime) + bahut heat. Whitewash mein Ca(OH)2 ka solution lagate hain; woh hawa ke CO2 se 2-3 din mein react karke CaCO3 (chamakta white layer) banata hai.

kb.question: What is electrolysis of water?
kb.answer: Acidified water mein electric current pass karo toh water tootta hai: 2H2O -> 2H2 + O2. Cathode pe hydrogen (double volume), anode pe oxygen. Ye electrolytic decomposition ka classic example hai.

kb.question: Why is AgCl stored in dark bottles?
kb.answer: AgCl sunlight mein toot jata hai (photolytic decomposition): 2AgCl -> 2Ag + Cl2 - grey silver ban jata hai. Isliye light se bachane ke liye dark coloured bottles mein rakhte hain.

kb.question: Heating ferrous sulphate?
kb.answer: Green ferrous sulphate crystals heat karne pe tootte hain: 2FeSO4 -> Fe2O3 + SO2 + SO3. Colour green se brown (Fe2O3) ho jata hai aur sulphur ke oxide gases nikalti hain. Thermal decomposition hai ye.
kb.source: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch.1, Activity 1.6 (Eq. 2FeSO4 -> Fe2O3 + SO2 + SO3)

teachTopics.name: Why do we balance equations?
teachTopics.juniorOpening: Bhaiya/didi, mujhe ye balancing samajh hi nahi aati. Equation aise hi likh do na, balance kyun karna hai?

points.text: Atoms can neither be created nor destroyed in a reaction (law of conservation of mass).
So each element must have equal atoms on both sides of the equation.
We balance by changing the numbers (coefficients) in front of formulas, never the formulas themselves.
An unbalanced equation is wrong because it breaks that law.

followUps: Par atoms kahan gaye phir? Reaction mein atoms toot te nahi kya?
Matlab left side aur right side same atoms? Ek example do na!
Number kahan change karte hain? Formula ke andar wale chhote number bhi badal sakte hain kya?
Agar balance na karo toh kya bigad jayega, seriously?
teachTopics.gotIt: OHHH! Ab samjha - atoms same rakhne hote hain dono side, isliye coefficients badalte hain. Tum toh teacher se bhi achhe samjhate ho!

teachTopics.name: Decomposition reactions and their types
teachTopics.juniorOpening: Yaar ye decomposition reaction kya hota hai? Aur uske types bhi hain?? Confused hu totally.

points.text: One reactant breaks down into two or more products.
Thermal decomposition uses heat, e.g. CaCO3 -> CaO + CO2.
Electrolytic decomposition uses electricity, e.g. 2H2O -> 2H2 + O2.
Photolytic decomposition uses light, e.g. 2AgCl -> 2Ag + Cl2.

followUps: Ek cheez toot ke alag alag ban jati hai? Example do na please!
Heat se kaise tootta hai? Koi real example?
Electricity se bhi toot sakta hai?? Kaise?
Aur light se? Seriously, dhoop se reaction hoti hai?
teachTopics.gotIt: Samajh gaya! Thermal = heat, electrolytic = current, photolytic = light - teeno mein ek reactant tootta hai. Kal exam mein pakka yaad rahega!

teachTopics.name: Exothermic vs endothermic
teachTopics.juniorOpening: Exo-endo mein hamesha confuse ho jata hu. Kaunsa heat deta hai, kaunsa leta hai? Simple mein batao na.

points.text: Exothermic reactions release heat/energy.
Examples: burning, respiration, quicklime + water.
Endothermic reactions absorb heat/energy.
Examples: thermal decomposition of CaCO3, photosynthesis.

followUps: Release matlab? Garam hota hai kya reaction? Example?
Respiration mein heat kaise nikalti hai, hum toh jalte nahi?
Toh endothermic mein thanda ho jata hai kya? Example batao na.
Photosynthesis mein heat kahan se aati hai?
teachTopics.gotIt: Exo = heat bahar, endo = heat andar! Respiration aur burning exo, CaCO3 ka decomposition endo. Easy tha ye toh, thanks!

teachTopics.name: Oxidation, reduction and redox
teachTopics.juniorOpening: Oxidation-reduction suna hai but kabhi samajh nahi aaya. Redox kya hota hai bhaiya/didi?

points.text: Oxidation = gain of oxygen or loss of hydrogen.
Reduction = loss of oxygen or gain of hydrogen.
Both happen together - that is why it is called a redox reaction.
Example: CuO + H2 -> Cu + H2O, CuO reduced, H2 oxidised.

followUps: Oxygen judna = oxidation? Toh reduction mein kya hota hai?
Dono ek saath kaise ho sakte hain? Ek hi reaction mein?
Ek example se samjhao na, formula wala!
Toh CuO + H2 wale mein kiska oxidation, kiska reduction?
teachTopics.gotIt: Aha! Oxidation aur reduction hamesha saath hote hain - isliye redox. CuO ka oxygen H2 ko mil gaya, sorted!

teachTopics.name: Corrosion, rusting and rancidity
teachTopics.juniorOpening: Cycle kyun rust ho jati hai aur chips kyun stale? Corrosion aur rancidity same hai kya?

points.text: Corrosion: metal slowly destroyed by reaction with air/moisture around it.
Rusting of iron: hydrated iron oxide Fe2O3.xH2O forms.
Prevention: painting, oiling, galvanisation.
Rancidity: oxidation of oils/fats in food; prevented by airtight packing, antioxidants, nitrogen flushing.

followUps: Metal hawa se react karta hai? Har metal?
Rust ka formula kya hai, exam mein aata hai kya?
Rust rokne ke liye kya kare? Ghar pe kya karte hain?
Aur chips packet mein nitrogen kyun bharte hain?
teachTopics.gotIt: Clear hai! Corrosion = metal ka kharab hona, rancidity = food ke fats ka oxidation. Dono oxidation hi hai basically!

explainers.title: Why your equation is 'wrong' even when it's right
explainers.hook: You wrote Mg + O2 -> MgO in the exam. Correct reaction, na? Still zero. The examiner's red pen didn't even blink.
explainers.concept: Atoms can't appear or vanish mid-reaction - that's the law of conservation of mass (NCERT Ch.1, §1.1.2). Mg + O2 -> MgO has 2 oxygens entering and only 1 leaving. An unbalanced equation claims matter vanished, so it's not an approximation, it's wrong. Balance with coefficients only: 2Mg + O2 -> 2MgO. Never touch the formula itself.
explainers.hack: Write the unbalanced equation first, then balance it as a separate visible step. Examiners award the balancing mark when they SEE the step. Doing it in your head hides your own mark.
explainers.hackSource: Visible step-by-step answers work like self-explanation - Make It Stick (Brown, Roediger & McDaniel, 2014).

explainers.title: The 4 reaction types are 4 dance moves
explainers.hook: Combination = two people become one couple. Decomposition = couple splits, both dance solo. Displacement = someone cuts in. Double displacement = everyone swaps partners.
explainers.concept: NCERT Ch.1 defines them by pattern: A+B->AB (combination, Eq. 1.13), AB->A+B (decomposition, Eq. 1.19-1.22), A+BC->AC+B (displacement, Activity 1.9), AB+CD->AD+CB (double displacement, Activity 1.10). Identify the PATTERN first, name the reaction second - never the other way round.
explainers.hack: Before the exam, take 10 random equations and sort them into the 4 patterns out loud. Sorting mixed types beats studying one type at a time - that's interleaving.
explainers.hackSource: Interleaving mixed practice improves discrimination between problem types - Make It Stick (Brown, Roediger & McDaniel, 2014).

explainers.title: Your body's heating bill: exo vs endo
explainers.hook: Ever touched a beaker when quicklime met water in the lab? It burns. That beaker was paying out heat like a heater with the window open.
explainers.concept: Exothermic = heat released along with products (NCERT Ch.1, after Eq. 1.17): burning, respiration (Eq. 1.18: glucose + oxygen -> CO2 + water + energy), CaO + water. Endothermic = heat absorbed: thermal decomposition of CaCO3, photosynthesis. Respiration is the classic trap - it FEELS like nothing is burning, but it releases energy, so it's exothermic.
explainers.hack: When a 'which is exothermic?' MCQ appears, physically recall the warm-beaker feeling for 5 seconds, then answer. Tying facts to a sensory memory makes them stickier.
explainers.hackSource: Linking new facts to concrete memories aids retrieval - Make It Stick (2014); retrieval itself strengthens memory (Roediger & Karpicke, Psychological Science, 2006).

explainers.title: The brown powder eating your cycle
explainers.hook: That reddish-brown powder on an old cycle isn't dirt. It's the iron literally reacting away into the air, molecule by molecule.
explainers.concept: Corrosion: a metal is attacked by substances around it - moisture, acids (NCERT Ch.1, §1.3.1). Rusting is iron's corrosion; silver blackens and copper turns green too. Rancidity is the food version: fats and oils get oxidised, smell and taste change (§1.3.2). Prevention from the same chapter: antioxidants, airtight containers, nitrogen-flushed chip bags.
explainers.hack: Rancidity's three preventions come as a 2-marker nearly every cycle. Recite them from memory right now without looking - if you can't, that's the one to revise tonight.
explainers.hackSource: Self-testing beats re-reading for long-term retention - Roediger & Karpicke, Psychological Science (2006); spacing over days - Ebbinghaus (1885).

learnMore.label: Khan Academy (Class 10 Science): corrosion and its prevention

explainers.title: Water splits, but only if you add a pinch of chemistry
explainers.hook: A student connects a battery to plain distilled water. Nothing happens. Bulb stays dark. The exam asks WHY - and 'no electricity' is not the answer.
explainers.concept: Distilled water is a poor conductor; a few drops of dilute H2SO4 make it conduct (NCERT Ch.1, Activity 1.7). Then: 2H2O -> 2H2 + O2, hydrogen at the cathode at DOUBLE the volume of oxygen at the anode. This was CBSE Sample Paper 2025-26 Q27, all three parts.
explainers.hack: Remember 'cathode = H2 = double'. One anchor fact, and the anode answer falls out free. Anchor facts beat re-reading whole paragraphs.
explainers.hackSource: Small retrieval anchors strengthen recall of linked facts - Roediger & Karpicke (2006).

explainers.title: One breaks into many, three different ways
explainers.hook: Limestone in a kiln, water under current, a photograph fading in sunlight - three unrelated scenes, one reaction type.
explainers.concept: Decomposition = one reactant breaks into two or more products (NCERT Ch.1, Eq. 1.19-1.22). The three triggers: HEAT (thermal: CaCO3 -> CaO + CO2; 2FeSO4 -> Fe2O3 + SO2 + SO3), ELECTRICITY (electrolytic: 2H2O -> 2H2 + O2), LIGHT (photolytic: 2AgCl -> 2Ag + Cl2, why photo films hate sunlight).
explainers.hack: Teach this to a friend (or our Junior) without notes. Explaining the three triggers with one example each is the fastest way to find out which one you actually don't know.
explainers.hackSource: Learning by teaching - Kobayashi meta-analysis (Japanese Psychological Research, 2019); the Feynman technique.
